summary: The team is juggling a critical Outlook account lockout, a knowledge website redesign, and a strategic pivot to prioritize China-based programs (Asia Star and Intelligent China) for marketing, with immediate follow-ups needed for the Tech in Asia Conference and Intelligent China webpage updates.
summaryDetail: Right now, the most urgent issue is the Outlook account lockout affecting multiple devices; the team must delete and re-login to update passwords, check mobile Outlook, and contact JSB to confirm the backend lock is lifted. In parallel, the knowledge website redesign is moving forward: Joseph needs to share the HTML design file, and he, Julie, and the speaker will meet to give specific feedback before Joker implements changes, combining elements from both concepts with a two-menu structure and integrated indices like BCI. On the marketing front, the team has decided to prioritize Asia Star and Intelligent China programs (with Berkeley as a third priority) for SEO and content optimization, while US programs are on hold; Joseph must draft target areas, analyze participant profiles, and get a brief on conversion tracking. This week also demands action on Tech in Asia Conference follow-ups: Alan Chen will add upcoming program lists to the thank-you email, Ben and Jay will create touch points for attendees, and Marcom will provide editing and graphic support. Looking ahead, Joseph needs to add website, SEM/SEO, GEO, and content plans to the work report by end of October, create three tabs for the Intelligent China webpage, and start updates, while the team continues to prioritize Module 1 for Intelligent China marketing and sales.

Include Berkeley program as a third priority for audit and potential marketing.
